name: Optimize integration test CI critical path

description: Validate retained two-shard CI stability on current HEAD; measurement could not find a CI run for the metadata-only commit.

asi.hypothesis: A further hosted-runner repeat will confirm the two-shard and shallow-diff gains without adding a third shard's compute cost.
asi.rollback_reason: The measurement script required an exact CI run for HEAD, but GitHub had not created a CI workflow run for the metadata-only commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Trigger or select the latest implementation-equivalent CI run explicitly, then rerun the CI measurement.

description: Re-measure the latest successful two-shard CI run; primary timing was valid, but the test-count parser double-counted the 379 Test Files as tests (2508 instead of 2129).

asi.hypothesis: A further hosted-runner measurement will confirm that two shards remain near the retained ~593s critical path.
asi.rollback_reason: Instrumentation matched `Integration Tests ... Test Files ... passed` as a test-summary line, so the required test-count guard was invalid even though both CI shards were green.
asi.next_action_hint: Anchor test-count parsing to the Vitest summary field after the log prefix, rerun against the same successful CI artifact, then establish a clean baseline because the initial crash recorded a zero metric.

description: Establish a valid GitHub Actions baseline for the retained two-shard CI setup: 599s critical path with all 379 files and 2,129 tests.

asi.hypothesis: The two-shard CI configuration remains stable near its prior ~593s mean while preserving the complete integration inventory.
asi.baseline_note: This is the first valid tool-recorded baseline; the apparent 0s best was the crash sentinel from a run that never found a CI workflow.

description: Reuse one PGlite database per SQL ORM test file while retaining per-test drop/recreate schema; focused files improved 29.85s to 10.99s, but the first full CI critical path regressed from 599s to 633s amid hosted-runner noise.

asi.hypothesis: Removing per-test PGlite startup from 32 SQL ORM files will reduce shard critical-path time without weakening per-test schema isolation.
asi.rollback_reason: The primary hosted CI metric was 34s slower than the valid 599s baseline on the first run, despite a 63% focused Vitest improvement and unchanged full inventory.
asi.next_action_hint: Repeat the same CI experiment once because prior retained sharded runs varied by 12s and this focused workload showed a large deterministic gain; keep only if the repeated primary metric beats baseline.

description: Confirmed per-file SQL ORM PGlite reuse on a second hosted run: critical path improved from the valid 599s baseline to 531s while all 379 files and 2,129 tests passed.

asi.hypothesis: Removing per-test PGlite startup from 32 SQL ORM files will reduce shard critical-path time without weakening per-test schema isolation.
asi.confirmation: Second hosted run improved primary by 68s (11.4%); focused four-file benchmark improved 29.85s to 10.99s and all 41 SQL ORM files / 315 tests passed.
asi.isolation: One database per Vitest file; existing drop/recreate schema still runs before every test.

description: Cache port PGlite databases by storage hash within each file; relation matrices improved locally from 69.80s to 20.07s, but the first hosted critical path was 548s versus the retained 531s best.

asi.hypothesis: Retaining one bounded PGlite database per storage contract will avoid repeated restarts in multi-contract relation matrices while preserving per-test truncation and forced replacement for transaction stress.
asi.rollback_reason: The first hosted primary metric regressed by 17s (3.2%) from the retained 531s best, although the maximum test step was only 3s slower and focused tests improved 71%.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect hosted per-file timings to verify whether both relation matrices improved, then repeat once if they did because runner/job overhead dominated this run; otherwise revert and pursue another hypothesis.

description: Repeat per-contract port database cache; relation matrices remained faster but the second hosted critical path regressed to 569s, so the change does not beat the retained 531s primary result.

asi.hypothesis: The large verified relation-matrix speedups will reduce the full CI critical path once hosted-runner import and unrelated-test variance normalize.
asi.rollback_reason: Two hosted runs measured 548s and 569s versus the retained 531s best; despite faster target files and full inventory, the primary metric did not improve on either run.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert the per-contract database cache, record the targeted idea in .auto/ideas.md for future reconsideration with better shard-level profiling, and pursue a different structural bottleneck such as sharding or CLI journey setup.

description: Shard the complete integration suite three ways: hosted critical path improved from the retained 531s best to 467s while preserving all 379 files and 2,129 tests.

asi.hypothesis: A third Vitest file shard will reduce the integration gate critical path without changing test behavior or inventory.
asi.confirmation: Three shards completed in 467s, 428s, and 364s with 127+126+126 files and 640+918+571 tests.
asi.tradeoff: A 12.1% critical-path reduction costs 24.4% more aggregate integration runner time versus the retained two-shard best.

description: Reapply per-contract Postgres port database reuse under three-way sharding: critical path improved from 467s to 462s and maximum test step from 392s to 369s with full inventory.

asi.hypothesis: With both alternating-contract relation matrices concentrated on the critical three-way shard, caching one PGlite database per storage hash will now reduce the full CI critical path.
asi.confirmation: Primary improved 5s (1.1%) and maximum test step improved 23s (5.9%); all 379 files and 2,129 tests passed.
asi.isolation: Rows are truncated before database reuse; transaction stress continues to force replacement.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect per-file and per-shard timings and repeat once because the primary gain is small relative to hosted-runner variance despite a stronger step-level improvement.

description: Shard the complete integration suite four ways: critical path improved from 462s to 324s and maximum test step from 369s to 273s with all tests preserved.

asi.hypothesis: A bounded fourth Vitest file shard will materially shorten the integration gate while preserving full behavior and maintaining a reasonable files-per-runner ratio.
asi.confirmation: Four shards completed in 324s, 297s, 285s, and 266s with 95+95+95+94 files and 598+495+604+432 tests.
asi.runner_cost_note: This hosted run used less aggregate runner time than the retained three-shard run despite the extra runner; treat the apparent compute saving as noise until repeated.

description: Confirm four-way integration sharding on an implementation-equivalent run: critical path improved again to 305s with full inventory, and aggregate runner time exactly matched the first four-shard run.

asi.hypothesis: A second four-shard hosted run will confirm the 324s result is structural rather than a favorable runner outlier.
asi.confirmation: Repeat completed in 305s critical path with jobs of 305s, 303s, 284s, and 280s; all 379 files and 2,129 tests passed.
asi.aggregate_stability: Aggregate integration runner time matched exactly across both four-shard runs.

description: Reuse one resettable PGlite server per ref/migration test file; focused tests improved 40.97s to 24.88s, but the first hosted critical path was 320s versus the retained 305s best.

asi.hypothesis: Resetting user-visible schemas on one PGlite server per file will eliminate 23 redundant startups while preserving fresh-database semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: The primary hosted metric regressed by 15s from the retained 305s best, despite a 39% focused improvement and unchanged full inventory.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect hosted timings for the two target files and repeat once if they improved, because 320s remains within the established 305–324s four-shard range.
asi.isolation: Drops non-system extensions and user schemas before every test; preserves _prisma_dev_* infrastructure and recreates the server on reset failure.

description: Shard integration tests five ways; maximum test step was essentially unchanged at 235s, while critical path regressed to 335s and aggregate runner time increased to 1,301s.

asi.hypothesis: A final bounded fifth shard will shorten the gate enough to justify its added runner overhead while preserving full inventory.
asi.rollback_reason: Critical path regressed from the retained 305s best to 335s; maximum test step improved only 2s, and aggregate runner time rose 11.0% from 1,172s to 1,301s.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert to four shards and stop increasing shard count; the fixed checkout/container/setup floor and uneven hosted-runner overhead now dominate.
